body:
I'm currently running into this issue and similar others with Godot's non standard approach to GLSL. Right now if I want to edit my GLSL in a proper IDE with syntax highlighting it chokes on the `#[compute]` directive, if I leave that out so I can edit the file properly I can't then have Godot compile the shader and tell me what's wrong with it, so I have to add it back in to satisfy Godot's not GLSL spec. 

**In case it wasn't obvious this is an utterly painful development experience for what is supposedly standard GLSL.** 

I'm not going to mince words here, this situation is entirely of Godot's creation and seemingly without any benefit. The docs say GLSL all over the place, but its not GLSL now is it? Few if any of the features the Godot team have added seem to justify breaking GLSL compatibility.

I appreciate that this is a matter of perspective, but I keep running into problems where there shouldn't be any had the shader just been standard GLSL, these header/directive problems is just the silliest of them.
